J. Ignacio Lucas Lledó & Mar Llaberia Robledillo

In 2025-11-06 bpp suggested the divergence between the two population is deeper than the average coalescence within any of the two populations. This is at odds with the analyses in 2025-07-09, where we prove that the effective number of different populations was not much larger than 1.0. The previous bpp results also contrast with SNAPPER’s analysis, run by Mar either including or excluding the admixed individuals.

The main difference between the bpp execution and previous results is that bpp was run in 2025-11-06 on the sequences found in 2023-05-17b/crepi95_outfiles/crepi95.alleles, which is one of the output files from ipyrad. In principle, those sequences are phased and called with a binomial model that incorporates global allele frequencies and an estimate of error rates (I think). So, they are not raw reads, and should not be plagued with sequencing errors. But, still, they were obtained by ipyrad with low coverage data. Chances are that they are less accurate than the genotypes called by ANGSD in 2025-03-15. To rule out the chance that input data biased bpp’s result in 2025-06-11, I will run it again with diploid sequences (instead of haplotypes) derived from the genotypes called with ANGSD in 2025-03-15.

Preparation of data files

In 2025-03-15 we have the following files:

  • toRad.geno: genotype matrix of RAD loci in 96 samples, coded as minor allele count (0, 1 or 2), with the value -1 for missing data.
  • toRef.geno: genotype matrix of reference-mapped loci in 96 samples.
  • toRad.mafs.gz: compressed list of RAD loci specifying the alleles present and which one is considered the minor one.
  • toRef.mafs.gz: same, for reference-mapped loci.
  • bamlist1.txt: list of BAM files mapped to the reference genome.
  • bamlist2.txt: list of BAM files mapped to the RAD loci.

We should also take into account the analyisis in 2025-06-12, where we found several loci suspected to be collapsed paralogous regions. To filter them out, a HWE test was run individually in each population. The inbreeding coefficient F reported in the .hwe.gz files was used to remove sites where all samples were heterozygous (\(F \simeq -1\)). I can use those reports, but the goal is to filter full loci, not individual sites, because collapsed paralogy, if real, must be a problem of the whole locus.

Collapsed paralogous loci revisited

# These are needed to remove collapsed paralogous loci:
if [ ! -e toRef.far.hwe ]; then
   gunzip -c ../2025-06-12/ref/SFS/unfiltered/farionis.hwe.gz > toRef.far.hwe
fi

if [ ! -e toRef.pse.hwe ]; then
   gunzip -c ../2025-06-12/ref/SFS/unfiltered/pseudofarionis.hwe.gz > toRef.pse.hwe
fi

if [ ! -e toRad.far.hwe ]; then
   gunzip -c ../2025-06-12/rad/SFS/unfiltered/farionis.hwe.gz > toRad.far.hwe
fi

if [ ! -e toRad.pse.hwe ]; then
   gunzip -c ../2025-06-12/rad/SFS/unfiltered/pseudofarionis.hwe.gz > toRad.pse.hwe
fi

I do not think there is any biological reason for such a relationship between allele frequency and deviation from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. Because both parameters were estimated jointly by maximum likelihood with ANGSD, I assume the relationship is an artifact of the method, maybe due to very low coverage. In any case, high MAF sites are a minority. We may not loose much by removing RAD loci containing sites with very negative inbreeding coefficients. The main discontinuity in the ECDF of the minimum F value per locus is at the lowest value, which justifies using the same threshold as in 2025-06-12.

Filtering of RAD loci

suppressMessages(library('dplyr'))
RadFarSum <- summarise(
   RadFarHwe,
   .by = Chromo,
   MinF   = min(F)
)

RadPseSum <- summarise(
   RadPseHwe,
   .by = Chromo,
   MinF   = min(F)
)

plot(ecdf(RadFarSum$MinF), main = c('Lowest F per locus'))
lines(ecdf(RadPseSum$MinF), col = 'blue')
legend(0.4, 0.4, c('C. farionis', 'C. pseudofarionis'),
                   lwd = 2, col = c('black', 'blue'), bty = 'n')

SelectedRadLoci <- intersect(
   RadFarSum[RadFarSum$MinF > min(RadFarSum$MinF), 'Chromo'],
   RadPseSum[RadPseSum$MinF > min(RadPseSum$MinF), 'Chromo'])

write(SelectedRadLoci, 'SelectedRadLoci.txt')

Following the estrategy in 2025-03-15, I subdivide reference contigs by loci, but I set the maximum gap length to only 100 (it was 1000 before). That is, contiguous sites are the same locus, long as it may be. And when a site with genotype data is more than 100 bases from the previous site with data, it becomes a new locus. I define loci within the 2025-03-15/toRef.geno file, which has the same coordinates as 2025-03-15/toRef.mafs.gz, and holds data from the two populations. However, the coordinates are different in toRef.far.hwe and toRef.pse.hwe, which hold the HWE information required to filter loci. It was difficult to transfer the locus information from the geno file to the hwes within R. When using coordinates of a hwe file as indices of the geno file, the assignment of locus values would neither fail nor finish, because R got stuck with non-existent indices. The way I do it below is to reduce the hwe files to only positions present in the geno file. Only then the assignment of values works fine.

Filtering of loci mapped to the reference genome

MaxDist <- 100
toRef.sample <- sub('.bam', '', basename(
  scan('../2025-03-15/bamlist1.txt',
       what = 'character', quiet = TRUE)))
GenoRef <- read.table('../2025-03-15/toRef.geno',
                      col.names = c('Contig', 'Pos', toRef.sample))
Map <- GenoRef[, c('Contig', 'Pos')]
n <- nrow(Map)
Map$Dist <- c(NA, Map[2:n, 'Pos'] - Map[1:(n - 1), 'Pos'])
previousContig <- c('NullContig',  Map[1:(n - 1), 'Contig'])
Map[Map$Chromo != previousContig, 'Dist'] <- NA
Map$Locus <- cumsum(is.na(Map$Dist) | Map$Dist > MaxDist)
row.names(Map) <- paste(Map$Contig, Map$Pos, sep = ':')

GenoRef$Locus <- Map$Locus

RFH <- RefFarHwe[paste(RefFarHwe$Chromo, RefFarHwe$Position, sep = ':') %in%
                    row.names(Map), ]
RFH$Locus <- Map[paste(RFH$Chromo,
                       RFH$Position,
                       sep = ':'), 'Locus']

RPH <- RefPseHwe[paste(RefPseHwe$Chromo, RefPseHwe$Position, sep = ':') %in%
                    row.names(Map), ]
RPH$Locus <- Map[paste(RPH$Chromo,
                       RPH$Position,
                       sep = ':'), 'Locus']

RefFarSum <- summarise(
   RFH,
   .by = Locus,
   MinF   = min(F)
)
RefPseSum <- summarise(
   RPH,
   .by = Locus,
   MinF   = min(F)
)
MapSum <- dplyr::summarise(Map, .by = Locus,
                    Contig = dplyr::first(Contig),
                    Start  = min(Pos),
                    End    = max(Pos))
write.table(MapSum, file = 'RefLoci.txt', quote = FALSE,
            sep = '\t', row.names = FALSE)

SelectedRefLoci <- intersect(
   RefFarSum[RefFarSum$MinF > min(RefFarSum$MinF), 'Locus'],
   RefPseSum[RefPseSum$MinF > min(RefPseSum$MinF), 'Locus']
)

Only 2600 are devoid of sites where all samples seem heterozygous in both populations.

Reconstruction of loci alignments

Recall that sequences used in SNAPPER were obtained by calling genotypes with ANGSD based on their posterior probabilities (2025-03-15). We used the -doGeno 2 flag in ANGSD, which produces genotypes coded by count of the minor allele (0, 1, 2) or -1 if the genotype is not called. Those genotypes are in 2025-03-15/toRad.geno and 2025-03-15/toRef.geno. The corresponding minor and major alleles are in 2025-03-15/to*.mafs files. The heterozygous positions should be turned to ambiguous IUPAC nucleotide codes (I think). The bpp program will use ambiguity codes if cleandata = 0 is in order.

if [ ! -e toRef.mafs ]; then
   gunzip -c ../2025-03-15/toRef.mafs.gz > toRef.mafs
fi
if [ ! -e toRad.mafs ]; then
   gunzip -c ../2025-03-15/toRad.mafs.gz > toRad.mafs
fi
devnull <- sapply(c('RadFarHwe', 'RadPseHwe', 'RefFarHwe', 'RefPseHwe',
                    'RadFarSum', 'RadPseSum', 'RefFarSum', 'RefPseSum'),
                  function(x) if (x %in% ls()) rm(x))

toRad.sample <- sub('.bam', '', basename(
  scan('../2025-03-15/bamlist2.txt',
       what = 'character', quiet = TRUE)))
all.equal(toRef.sample, toRad.sample)
## [1] TRUE
MafsRef <- read.table('toRef.mafs', header = TRUE)
stopifnot(all.equal(GenoRef$Contig, MafsRef$chromo))
stopifnot(all.equal(GenoRef$Pos,    MafsRef$position))
MafsRef$Locus <- Map$Locus
GenoRef <- GenoRef[GenoRef$Locus %in% SelectedRefLoci, ]

GenoRad <- read.table('../2025-03-15/toRad.geno',
                      col.names = c('Locus', 'Pos', toRad.sample))
GenoRad <- GenoRad[GenoRad$Locus %in% SelectedRadLoci, ]
MafsRad <- read.table('toRad.mafs', header = TRUE)

GeneticIds <- read.table('../2024-10-05/summary.txt', header = TRUE)
GeneticIds$species <- ifelse(GeneticIds$K2.1 > 0.95, 'pseudofarionis', 'unknown')
GeneticIds$species <- ifelse(GeneticIds$K2.2 > 0.95, 'farionis', GeneticIds$species)
farionis <- GeneticIds[GeneticIds$species == 'farionis',       'Sample']
pseudofa <- GeneticIds[GeneticIds$species == 'pseudofarionis', 'Sample']
minCount2Seq <- function(x, minor, major){
   # Intended to turn one vector of minor counts (for one locus)
   # into a string of nucleotides, knowning the minor and major
   # alleles at those sites.
   stopifnot(is.numeric(x))
   stopifnot(all(x >= -1))
   stopifnot(all(x <= 2))
   stopifnot(length(x) == length(minor))
   stopifnot(length(minor) == length(major))
   x <- x + 2
   hets <- Biostrings::mergeIUPACLetters(paste0(minor, major))
   Code <- cbind(rep('-', length(x)), major, hets, minor)
   Seq <- paste0(mapply(function(i, j) Code[i, j], 1:length(x), x),
                 collapse = '')
   return(Seq)
}

if (! file.exists('crepiRad.phy')) {
   phyfile = file('crepiRad.phy', 'w')
   devnull <- lapply(
      SelectedRadLoci,
      function(x) {
         Minor <- MafsRad[MafsRad$chromo == x, 'minor']
         Major <- MafsRad[MafsRad$chromo == x, 'major']
         Genos <- GenoRad[GenoRad$Locus == x, ]
         if (length(Minor) > 25) {
            Seqs <- lapply(
               toRad.sample,
               function(y) {
                  s <- minCount2Seq(Genos[, y], Minor, Major)
                  if (stringr::str_count(s, '-') < 0.25 * nchar(s)) {
                     return(s)
                  } else {
                     return(NULL)
                  }
               }
            )
            names(Seqs) <- toRad.sample
            Seqs <- Seqs[! sapply(Seqs, is.null)]
            NumFar <- sum(names(Seqs) %in% farionis)
            NumPse <- sum(names(Seqs) %in% pseudofa)
            if ((NumFar > 1) & (NumPse > 1)) {
               Seqs <- Seqs[names(Seqs) %in% c(farionis, pseudofa)]
               cat(paste0(length(Seqs), ' ', length(Minor), '\n'),
                   file = phyfile, append = TRUE)
               for (i in 1:length(Seqs)) {
                  cat(paste0(x, '^', names(Seqs)[i], '   ', Seqs[i], '\n'),
                      file = phyfile, append = TRUE)
               }
            }
         }
      })
   close(phyfile)
}

if (! file.exists('crepiRef.phy')) {

      SelectedRefLoci,

         Major <- MafsRef[MafsRef$Locus == x, 'major']

         if (length(Minor) > 25) {

                  if (stringr::str_count(s, '-') < 0.25 * nchar(s)) {
                     return(s)
                  } else {
                     return(NULL)
                  }
               }
            )
            names(Seqs) <- toRef.sample
            Seqs <- Seqs[! sapply(Seqs, is.null)]
            NumFar <- sum(names(Seqs) %in% farionis)
            NumPse <- sum(names(Seqs) %in% pseudofa)
            if ((NumFar > 1) & (NumPse > 1)) {
               Seqs <- Seqs[names(Seqs) %in% c(farionis, pseudofa)]
               cat(paste0(length(Seqs), ' ', length(Minor), '\n'),
                   file = phyfile, append = TRUE)
               for (i in 1:length(Seqs)) {
                  cat(paste0(x, '^', names(Seqs)[i], '   ', Seqs[i], '\n'),
                      file = phyfile, append = TRUE)
               }
            }
         }
      })
   close(phyfile)
}

Running bpp

The bpp will not be able to use loci with too many samples or with too many variable sites, because now we are using diploid sequences, which need to be phased, and bpp considers every possible combination of alleles along heterozygous sites of a locus. Before preparing the control files, I need to reduce the data set and select up to 7 sequences per population.

Loci have in general unexpectedly high average fraction of heterozygous sites per sequence (not shown). I apply some arbitrary filter for excess of heterozygosity just to facilitate bpp’s job. Inevitably, this introduces a bias: we will estimate population parameters from sites chosen to be less variable.

Below I use the functions rand() and asorti() in gawk to randomly choose a few sequences from each population. The dataset from alignments to the reference does not seem good enough. From RAD loci I generate a third data file with up to 4 sequences per population and including 2, 3 or 4 sequences from lake Bienne, which are suspected to be C. metoecus.

Data file reduction

# "A" is C. farionis, "B" is C. pseudofarionis and C...
if [ ! -e imap.txt ]; then
   tail -n +2 ../2024-10-05/summary.txt | \
   gawk '($3 > 0.95){
      print $1 "\tA"
   }($2 > 0.95){
      print $1 "\tB"
   }' > imap.txt
   echo -e "N044Cx2\tC" >> imap.txt
   echo -e "N048Cma\tC" >> imap.txt
   echo -e "N048Cmb\tC" >> imap.txt
   echo -e "N048Cmc\tC" >> imap.txt
fi

if [ ! -e crepiRad2.phy ]; then
   gawk -v MAXHET=3 '(FILENAME == "imap.txt"){
      SP[$1] = $2
   }(/\^/){
      split($1, A, /\^/)
      LOC = A[1]
      SMP = A[2]
      SEQ[A[2]] = $2
      HET = gsub(/[YRMKSW]/, "n", $2)
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "A")) {
         NUMA += 1
         ORDA[sprintf("%.0f", rand() * 10000)] = A[2]
         asorti(ORDA, NEWA)
      }
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "B")) {
         NUMB += 1
         ORDB[sprintf("%.0f", rand() * 10000)] = A[2]
         asorti(ORDB, NEWB)
      }
      if (HET == MAXHET) WARN++ 
   }(/^[0-9]+ [0-9]+$/){
      if ((NUMA >= 7) && (NUMB >= 7) && (WARN < 4)) {
         print "14 " length(SEQ[SMP])
         for (i = 1; i <= 7; i++) {
            SA = ORDA[NEWA[i]]
            SB = ORDB[NEWB[i]]
            print LOC "^" SA "   " SEQ[SA]
            print LOC "^" SB "   " SEQ[SB]
         }
      }
      delete SEQ
      delete ORDA
      delete ORDB
      delete NEWA
      delete NEWB
      NUMA = 0
      NUMB = 0
      WARN = 0
   }' imap.txt crepiRad.phy > crepiRad2.phy
fi

if [ ! -e crepiRef2.phy ]; then
   gawk -v MAXHET=4 '(FILENAME == "imap.txt"){
      SP[$1] = $2
   }(/\^/){
      split($1, A, /\^/)
      LOC = A[1]
      SMP = A[2]
      SEQ[A[2]] = $2
      HET = gsub(/[YRMKSW]/, "n", $2)
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "A")) {
         NUMA += 1
         ORDA[sprintf("%.0f", rand() * 10000)] = A[2]
         asorti(ORDA, NEWA)
      }
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "B")) {
         NUMB += 1
         ORDB[sprintf("%.0f", rand() * 10000)] = A[2]
         asorti(ORDB, NEWB)
      }
      if (HET == MAXHET) WARN++ 
   }(/^[0-9]+ [0-9]+$/){
      if ((NUMA >= 7) && (NUMB >= 7) && (WARN < 5)) {
         print "14 " length(SEQ[SMP])
         for (i = 1; i <= 7; i++) {
            SA = ORDA[NEWA[i]]
            SB = ORDB[NEWB[i]]
            print LOC "^" SA "   " SEQ[SA]
            print LOC "^" SB "   " SEQ[SB]
         }
      }
      delete SEQ
      delete ORDA
      delete ORDB
      delete NEWA
      delete NEWB
      NUMA = 0
      NUMB = 0
      WARN = 0
   }' imap.txt crepiRef.phy > crepiRef2.phy
fi

if [ ! -e crepiRad3.phy ]; then
   gawk -v MAXHET=15 '(FILENAME == "imap.txt"){
      SP[$1] = $2
   }(/\^/){
      split($1, A, /\^/)
      LOC = A[1]
      SMP = A[2]
      SEQ[A[2]] = $2
      HET = gsub(/[YRMKSW]/, "n", $2)
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "A")) {
         NUMA += 1
         ORDA[sprintf("%.0f", rand() * 10000)] = A[2]
         asorti(ORDA, NEWA)
      }
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "B")) {
         NUMB += 1
         ORDB[sprintf("%.0f", rand() * 10000)] = A[2]
         asorti(ORDB, NEWB)
      }
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "C")) {
         NUMC += 1
         ORDC[NUMC] = A[2]
      }
      if (HET == MAXHET) WARN++ 
   }(/^[0-9]+ [0-9]+$/){
      if ((NUMA >= 4) && (NUMB >= 4) && (NUMC >= 1) && (WARN < 10)) {
         print 4 + 4 + NUMC " " length(SEQ[SMP])
         for (i = 1; i <= 4; i++) {
            SA = ORDA[NEWA[i]]
            SB = ORDB[NEWB[i]]
            print LOC "^" SA "   " SEQ[SA]
            print LOC "^" SB "   " SEQ[SB]
         }
         for (i in ORDC) {
            print LOC "^" ORDC[i] "   " SEQ[ORDC[i]]
         }
      }
      delete SEQ
      delete ORDA
      delete ORDB
      delete ORDC
      delete NEWA
      delete NEWB
      delete NEWC
      NUMA = 0
      NUMB = 0
      NUMC = 0
      WARN = 0
   }' imap.txt crepiRad.phy > crepiRad3.phy
fi

Unfortunately, crepiRad3.phy is empty. Aparently, there are no loci with at least four sequences of C. farionis, four of C. pseudofarionis and two C. metoecus.

One species

if [ ! -e template.ctl ]; then
   echo "seed = -1"                                > template.ctl
   echo "seqfile = input.phy"                     >> template.ctl
   echo "Imapfile = imap.txt"                     >> template.ctl
   echo "jobname = out.txt"                       >> template.ctl
   echo "speciesdelimitation = 0"                 >> template.ctl
   echo "speciestree = 0"                         >> template.ctl
   echo "species&tree = 2 A B"                    >> template.ctl
   echo "                 7 7  * maxseqs"         >> template.ctl
   echo "               (A,B); * guidetree"       >> template.ctl
   echo "phase = 1 1"                             >> template.ctl
   echo "usedata = 1"                             >> template.ctl
   echo "nloci = 1000"                            >> template.ctl
   echo "alphaprior = 1 1 4"                      >> template.ctl
   echo "cleandata = 0"                           >> template.ctl
   echo "thetaprior = 3 0.04 e"                   >> template.ctl
   echo "tauprior = 3 0.01"                       >> template.ctl
   echo "locusrate = 1 0 0 5.0 iid"               >> template.ctl
   echo "clock = 1"                               >> template.ctl
   echo "finetune = 1"                            >> template.ctl
   echo "print = 1 0 0 0 0"                       >> template.ctl
   echo "burnin = 25000"                          >> template.ctl
   echo "sampfreq = 250"                          >> template.ctl
   echo "nsample = 100000"                        >> template.ctl
   echo "threads = 8 25 1"                        >> template.ctl
fi

if [ ! -e onesp1.ctl ]; then
   cp template.ctl onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/Imapfile =/c * Imapfile = imap.txt"   onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/seqfile = /c seqfile = crepiRad2.phy" onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/jobname = /c jobname = onesp/out1"    onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/species&tr/c species&tree = 1 A"      onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/ * maxseqs/c            14 * maxseqs" onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/ * guidetr/c               * guidetr" onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/phase = /c phase = 1"                 onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/finetune =/c finetune = 1 Gage:99.000000 Gspr:0.001216 th1:0.000382 tau:0.000000 mix:0.041259 alfa:2.638333 mu_i:0.867624" onesp1.ctl
fi

if [ ! -e onesp2.ctl ]; then
   cp onesp1.ctl onesp2.ctl
   sed -i "/jobname = /c jobname = onesp/out2"    onesp2.ctl
   sed -i "/threads = /c threads = 8 17 1"        onesp2.ctl
fi

if [ ! -d onesp ]; then mkdir onesp; fi
if [ ! -e onesp/out1.txt ]; then
   bpp --cfile onesp1.ctl 1> onesp/out1.log 2> onesp/out1.err &
fi
if [ ! -e onesp/out2.txt ]; then
   bpp --cfile onesp2.ctl 1> onesp/out2.log 2> onesp/out2.err &
fi
wait

This was finally run from run1.sh, but it’s the same.

The two chains were meant to run for 50 million generations, sampled every 500 generations. They run to around 20 million generations, and yieled around 40000 samples each. In Garnatxa, we run again the two chains with different priors (inverted gamma, instead of gamma), for 15 million generations, sampled every 500 generations.

Two isolated species

In order to be able to manipulate the README.Rmd file while performing the analysis, and also to parallellize the runs, I run the following block from an independent scripts run2.sh.

if [ ! -e imap2.txt ]; then
   grep -v -P "\tC$" imap.txt > imap2.txt
fi
if [ ! -d twosp ]; then mkdir twosp; fi
if [ ! -e twosp1.ctl ]; then
   cp template.ctl twosp1.ctl
   sed -i "/seqfile = /c seqfile = crepiRad2.phy"    twosp1.ctl
   sed -i "/Imapfile =/c Imapfile = imap2.txt"       twosp1.ctl
   sed -i "/jobname = /c jobname = twosp/out1"       twosp1.ctl
   sed -i "/finetune =/c finetune = 1" twosp1.ctl
fi

if [ ! -e twosp2.ctl ]; then
   cp twosp1.ctl twosp2.ctl
   sed -i "/jobname = /c jobname = twosp/out2"       twosp2.ctl
   sed -i "/threads = /c threads = 8 17 1"           twosp2.ctl
fi

if [ ! -e twosp/out1.txt ]; then
   bpp --cfile twosp1.ctl 1> twosp/out1.log 2> twosp/out1.err &
fi

if [ ! -e twosp/out2.txt ]; then
   bpp --cfile twosp2.ctl 1> twosp/out2.log 2> twosp/out2.err &
fi
wait

The model with two isolated species was run only in Thermomix, with gamma instead of inverted gamma priors. It is not strictly necessary, because we can compare the two species model with and without migration using the Savage-Dickey ratio from the posterior of the model with migration.

   sed -i "/ * maxseqs/c                  4 4 4"      threesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/ * guidetr/c             ((A,B),C);"      threesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/phase = /c phase = 1 1 1"                 threesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/finetune =/c finetune = 1" threesp1.ctl
fi

if [ ! -e threesp2.ctl ]; then
   cp threesp1.ctl threesp2.ctl
   sed -i "/jobname = /c jobname = threesp/out2"      threesp2.ctl
   sed -i "/threads = /c threads = 8 17 1"            threesp2.ctl
fi

if [ ! -e threesp/out1.txt ]; then
   bpp --cfile threesp1.ctl 1> threesp/out1.log 2> threesp/out1.err &
fi

if [ ! -e threesp/out2.txt ]; then
   bpp --cfile threesp2.ctl 1> threesp/out2.log 2> threesp/out2.err &
fi
wait

Two species with migration

The following was run from run3.sh. In addition, I created run4.sh in order to run the same model without data, just to check the priors.

if [ ! -d twoMig ]; then mkdir twoMig; fi
if [ ! -e twoMig1.ctl ]; then
   cp template.ctl twoMig1.ctl
   sed -i "/seqfile = /c seqfile = crepiRad2.phy"    twoMig1.ctl
   sed -i "/jobname = /c jobname = twoMig/out1"      twoMig1.ctl
   sed -i "/phase = /c *newline  \nphase = 1 1"      twoMig1.ctl
   sed -i "/*newline /c migprior = 2 200\n*newline " twoMig1.ctl
   sed -i "/*newline /c migration 2\n  A B\n  B A"   twoMig1.ctl
fi
if [ ! -e twoMig2.ctl ]; then
   cp twoMig1.ctl twoMig2.ctl
   sed -i "/jobname = /c jobname = twoMig/out2"      twoMig2.ctl
   sed -i "/threads = /c threads = 8 17 1"           twoMig2.ctl
fi

if [ ! -e twoMig/out1.txt ]; then
   bpp --cfile twoMig1.ctl 1> twoMig/out1.log 2> twoMig/out1.err &
fi
if [ ! -e twoMig/out2.txt ]; then
   bpp --cfile twoMig2.ctl 1> twoMig/out2.log 2> twoMig/out2.err &
fi
wait

The model of two species with migration was run both in Thermomix (with gramma priors, as detailed above) and in Garnatxa (with inverse gamma priors). Details of the Garnatxa run are saved in the folder Garnatxa.

Three species with migration between two of them

This could not be run, for the same reason as above.

fi

Analysis of results

I move the analysis of results to a new folder.

One species

source('mcmc.R')
mcmc1 <- read.table('onesp/out1.mcmc.txt', header = TRUE)
mcmc2 <- read.table('onesp/out2.mcmc.txt', header = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
autocorPlot(mcmc1)
autocorPlot(mcmc2)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
tendencyPlot(mcmc1)

tendencyPlot(mcmc2)

convergencePlot(mcmc1, mcmc2)

onesp <- rbind(mcmc1, mcmc2)
plot(density(onesp$theta.1.A, bw = 'SJ'), main = expression(theta[A]))
abline(v = mean(onesp$theta.1.A), col = 'red', lty = 2)
text(0.015, 1000, sprintf("Mean = %.4f\nS.D. = %.4f",
                           mean(onesp$theta.1.A),
                           sd(onesp$theta.1.A)))
